constraints: Offline exact-byte JSON snapshot pinned by the caller; at most sixteen direct peers, sixteen issuers per peer and three allowed capability names per row.
Validate every row, including unselected peers; require local/remote identity, exclusive expiry and caller revision floor before composing public bundle verification.
No policy authoring language, hierarchy, transitive trust, enrollment, network service or target hardware deadline is specified.
alternatives: CPython explicit closed-table validation using shared lexical admission and public bundle verification.
Cedar policy language and typed principal/action/resource authorization model.
OPA/Rego structured-data policy evaluation with a separate exact-byte lexical boundary.
Rust typed structures and explicit validators using the same versioned JSON profile.
rationale: KEEP the closed-table validator: the small fixed relation can be checked completely without introducing policy-language evaluation or entity-hierarchy semantics. Exact-byte parsing and canonical equality remain explicit.

Cedar and Rego are credible dedicated policy technologies when policy authoring and richer relationships are required; neither replaces input encoding validation, caller authentication or revision-floor persistence.

Rust can express the same closed relation. No target workload or allocation/deadline contract establishes a material native advantage for this offline metadata boundary; no comparative speed claim is made.
Eleven direct-federation methods and four composition methods pass, covering malformed unselected rows, direct scope, expiry, revocation and caller floors. No production mismatch was demonstrated.
limits: Caller pins, clock and revision floor require external provenance. A saved successful result is ordinary metadata and is not revoked in place.
Current comparison is source-based, not an executed full alternate implementation. No winning migration is deferred.
No transport, distributed consensus, anti-replay persistence, MLS/CNSA accreditation or availability evidence.
